# Interests, education and an affordable life

Release 0.35.1 · October 18, 2026

Keep the student's interest matches. Show realistic ways forward when starting pay falls short. No extra questionnaire was added.

## What students see

- Clear education badges on career matches, career details, the reading library and the personal plan.
- Related jobs with starting pay and an Austin lifestyle comparison.
- Five routes to compare: workplace learning, apprenticeship, community college or specialist training, bachelor's degree, and graduate/professional study.
- An explicit distinction between supported matches and related work that needs exploration.
- More info for exact preparation, training pay, later-pay illustrations and the method.

A college degree is presented through concrete related jobs it could open. It does not add points to a student's interest score or automatically raise the wage for the same occupation. Nursing's ADN and BSN routes use the same RN wage reference. The default ADN budget is not presented as a BSN price.

## How the additional options are chosen

The original six-score assessment and profession matching do not change. A separate comparison layer uses shared career fields, O*NET detailed interest areas, relevant knowledge, the complete interest pattern and answered profession questions. Known work or clinical-route conflicts exclude suggested alternatives. A single broad subject such as engineering cannot by itself send a carpenter toward biomedical engineering. A few editorial task bridges connect personal styling or tattoo art to visual-design work, but only when a separate positive creative-field interest and a compatible overall profile support exploration. These bridges are labeled as related ideas, not validated correlations. Broad comparisons are marked as such; they are not new confirmed matches.

We order related work by its connection to the student's interests, then identify the options whose pay could cover the chosen budget. Income and education do not improve the interest score. If no suitable starting-pay alternative covers the goal, the screen shows the closest related comparisons and labels any later-pay scenario as an illustration. We do not invent a high-paying match, a career at each education level, or a guaranteed promotion.

The five levels compare different jobs and sometimes legitimate alternative entry routes. They do not imply that adding degrees produces automatic salary steps within one job. Some management roles require related work experience; they are not offered as first-job income solutions.

## Financial interpretation

Salary sources remain the existing Austin references, including clearly identified regional proxies and published employer examples. A regional starting-wage proxy is not the same sample as one apprenticeship's pay schedule; an apprentice example can exceed that regional proxy. We keep both labels and do not force an artificial monotonic comparison.

The budget includes the same taxes, savings, recurring costs and entered loan payments used elsewhere in Fieldguide. A green comparison requires both a nonnegative monthly balance and a displayed salary at least as high as the displayed starting-income target. This avoids a rounding contradiction such as “$60K covers a $65K goal.” Upfront home-buying cash and unchosen future borrowing remain separate. More info points to the job's study costs, funding and loan budget. Grants, loans and scholarships are not invented to make a route affordable.

Later 5/10/20-year pay remains a planning illustration unless a published employer schedule is specifically identified. “Could cover” is a budget comparison, not a prediction that a student will earn that amount or obtain that job.

## Checks and limits

All 148 public frozen-life cases were replayed with unchanged answers, six scores and original career matches. Related alternatives, route badges and budget comparisons were checked separately. Six owner-only cases were checked locally without adding their histories to the public files. Developer model reviews can preview alternative plans without changing a real student's saved guide. Reruns use the edited copy; reset restores the original.

The review found and tightened an overly broad cross-field link. Existing completed steps and notes survive a new career preview. Phone checks cover compact cards, readable text, disclosures, alternative links and an isolated plan comparison. No claims of real-student accuracy, clinical assessment or validated earnings prediction follow from these fictional replays.

See the accompanying opportunity replay JSON for the actual case counts and per-case alternatives. It records a regression review, not a newly independent holdout evaluation.

## Source basis

- [BLS: Education and training assignments by occupation](https://www.bls.gov/emp/tables/education-summary.htm). Typical entry preparation is occupation-specific; it is not a promise about a person's earnings.
- [BLS: Field of degree](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/field-of-degree/home.htm). A subject can connect to several occupations.
- [Registered Apprenticeship: Career seekers](https://www.apprenticeship.gov/career-seekers). Paid work, mentoring, classroom learning and credentials are distinct from an immediate qualified wage.
- [U.S. Department of Labor: Educational level and pay](https://www.dol.gov/general/topic/wages/educational). Broad earnings associations do not establish a same-job salary premium or a guaranteed personal return.

No new external service, billing account or private-model access rule was added or changed.
